items.text: Houshang Hassan-Yari, a Middle East and military affairs expert, considered the statements attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei as a reflection of recent threats by the IRGC and said there is a gap between these threats and the operational capability of the Islamic Republic, and these statements do not create deterrence.

Tasnim reported that a delegation from Iran has traveled to Doha but no negotiations with the US in Qatar are underway, and the Iranian delegation's presence is to advance recent talks with Qatar. Axios reported that Qatari mediators led by Ali Al-Thawadi are still negotiating in Doha with the Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister and are regularly in contact with the White House. No agreement has yet been reached to resume direct negotiations between the US and Iran, and no date has been set for the US delegation to arrive in Doha.

Iranian director Bahman Ghobadi said at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival that the Islamic Republic has separated him from his home, family, and friends for 19 years and forced him into exile. He made these remarks in response to an Iran International reporter's question about the connection between the theme of his latest film and his personal relationship with Iran. Ghobadi is participating in the festival with his film "The Trees Are Watching."

Abbas Araghchi said there is currently no plan to meet with American officials and speculations are only media-based. He added that the Islamic Republic's conditions are clear and mediators are negotiating them. Araghchi also mentioned the review of JD Vance's message and the dispatch of a delegation to Doha.

Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst, said that displaying life and joy in the streets is a form of social resistance and that the Islamic Republic has a problem with the life people build based on their own will and choice.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, told Al Jazeera that Tehran does not rule out any possibility of war and is prepared for all scenarios. He added that the Islamic Republic has modernized its weapons and its forces are at the highest level of readiness. Araghchi also said Tehran seeks recognition of the new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz and that mediators have presented proposals on the nuclear file which Tehran is reviewing.

A video released on social media shows the mother of Amir Mohammad Hatami shouting while holding up a picture of her son, asking for what crime her innocent son was killed. Amir Mohammad Hatami, an 18-year-old from Shahin Shahr, Isfahan, was shot in the right eye and killed after being wounded and arrested on the evening of January 9.

Ahmad Mohammadzadeh Javan, Iran's representative in the 61 kg weight class, won the final of the World Freestyle Wrestling Championships with a score of 9-2 against Zaur Uguev, the world and Olympic champion from Russia, and earned the gold medal. This is the first gold medal for Iran's national freestyle wrestling team in this year's competitions.

On the third day of the 2026 World Wrestling Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan, Iran's 79kg wrestler Mohammad Nokhodi became a finalist by defeating Jabrayil Gadzhiev from Azerbaijan. He will be Iran's only finalist on the last day. Additionally, Amir Mohammad Yazdani and Milad Valizadeh returned to the repechage bracket, and Amirhossein Firouzpour advanced to the ranking round.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces, announced the update of the enemy target database, stating that these targets are now in a wider geographical area. He emphasized that the armed forces will respond immediately and effectively if signs of hostile action are observed, with no geographical limitation. Abdollahi warned that the US and Israel will face a response harsher and more effective than the previous war.

Shahrouz Sadidi, a resident of Sabzevar, has been held in the city's prison without a clear decision for over a month, and his detention order has been extended for another month. He has been kept in solitary confinement in the quarantine section of Sabzevar prison for 32 days, and his family and lawyers have not been able to access his case file. Judicial officials have not provided clear answers to his family.

Amirhossein Zare won the second gold medal for Iranian freestyle wrestling at the 2026 World Championship in Astana, Kazakhstan, by defeating Abdullah Kurbanov from Russia 11-0 in the 125 kg final. Earlier, Ahmad Mohammadzadeh Javan won the gold medal in the 61 kg category. Zare scored 42 points in the competition and did not concede any points to his opponents.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Eje'i, head of the Judiciary of the Islamic Republic, called for speeding up the handling of cases of Iranians living abroad who, according to him, have acted against the Islamic Republic. He also called for quick handling of cases of individuals who, according to him, "gave information to the enemy."

Iranians in Stockholm, in the eleventh month of their continuous gatherings, demanded the overthrow of the Islamic Republic and commemorated the martyrs. One participant said that Iranians abroad are the voice of the people and prisoners in Iran and urged people not to lose hope.

A video received by Iran International shows that Iranians in Finland on Saturday supported the national revolution and Prince Reza Pahlavi during a march commemorating Cyrus the Great, chanting: "The king is coming to his country, all of Iran is behind him."

Valiollah Bayati, spokesperson for the Parliament's Councils Commission, said a decisive, proportionate, and deterrent response must be given to every hostile act by enemies, and the cost of aggression must be increased for the enemy. He added that for every target hit, 10 targets must be struck in return and emphasized that strategic capacities of the country, including the Strait of Hormuz, must not be lost. Bayati also referred to the difficult living conditions of the people and called on officials to focus on securing national interests both militarily and diplomatically.

Houthi forces supported by the Islamic Republic in Yemen released images on Saturday, 9 Aban, which they said show their forces repelling Saudi Arabian military reinforcements and destroying several military vehicles in the east of Al-Jawf province in northern Yemen.

Herana News Agency reported that the assets of the Inverse Art Academy and its founder, Alireza Ardoubadi, have been seized and the process of confiscation is ongoing. The academy's website has been filtered and its bank accounts and payment gateways have been blocked. Fars News Agency cited accusations of "propaganda against the regime" and "insulting Shia" against Ardoubadi as the reason for these actions.

Mohammad Mohahedi Azad, the Attorney General, said that all damages caused to the country will be collected jointly from the United States, Israel, and any country that cooperated in hostility against the Islamic Republic. He added that countries that helped enemies against the people and the Islamic Republic have fallen into pits they dug for Iran.

Zeinab Soleimani, a pediatric specialist, has been detained since Farvardin of this year in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan and has spent most of her detention in solitary confinement. She has been hospitalized three times at Farabi Psychiatric Hospital in Isfahan, and her mental health has severely deteriorated. No court session has been held for her case, and she remains in uncertainty.

Fars News Agency reported that the assets of Alireza Ardoubadi, owner of the Inverse school and training center, have been seized and are being confiscated. Fars wrote that this individual insulted Shiites and promoted against the regime on his social media pages. By order of judicial authorities, all payment gateways and bank accounts of the Inverse training center have been deactivated.

Persepolis football team defeated Nassaji Mazandaran 1-0 in the eleventh week of the Iranian Premier League, reaching 23 points and returning to the top of the table. Mohammad Mehdi Mohebi scored the only goal of the match in the 58th minute. Mehdi Tartar's team is at the top of the table due to a better goal difference than Sepahan.
Iranians in Sweden marched on Saturday, 9 Aban, continuing protests in support of the national revolution and chanted: "Pahlavi is my voice."

Mohammad Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that since 1366 they have planned to control the Strait of Hormuz and their goal is to completely remove the United States from the region. He added that they have no hesitation in confronting the opposing side and that in case of the slightest action by the enemy, the Islamic Republic's response must be swift, decisive, and stronger than before.

Israel's Channel 11 reported that the US government informed Gulf countries that Mojtaba Khamenei ordered senior military commanders to respond to a possible attack on Iran immediately, effectively, and without geographical limitations.

A video received by Iran International shows that on Saturday, 9 Aban, a gathering was held in front of the Embassy of the Islamic Republic in London in support of the people of Iran and their national revolution.

Shayan Shakibaie, 29, who was arrested in Kerman during the nationwide protests of January 2026, was reportedly sentenced to death by Branch 5 of the Kerman Revolutionary Court. In the same case, three other defendants were collectively sentenced to 28 years in prison, with Mohammad Hosseiniyani receiving 12 years and two other defendants each receiving eight years. No precise information has been released yet regarding the charges attributed to Shakibaie or the evidence cited by the court.

Protesters gathered in Paris on Saturday, 9 Aban, and said they would continue to be present in the streets until their demands are met. This gathering took place as France was preparing for another round of protests; French officials had warned that these protests might turn violent.
A video received by Iran International shows a citizen installing a picture of Cyrus the Great in a school classroom simultaneously with his commemorative day.

A garden hall in Robat Karim was sealed following a Halloween party due to what the public places supervision police described as "non-compliance with disciplinary regulations and Islamic norms." The owner of this business unit was also referred to the judiciary.

Donald Trump, President of the United States, said in an interview that the issue of Cuba will be resolved within two years. He added that they will first finish the Iran issue and then move on to Cuba. Trump also said that Marco Rubio is examining the issue very carefully and that his parents are from Cuba.

Protesting youth gathered on Saturday, 9 Aban, in front of the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin following a call by the "GenZ regelt" movement for nationwide protests in Germany. Thousands of young people are expected to take to the streets in more than 30 German cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt, and Cologne.

Iman Aghayari, a political analyst, considered the statements attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei as a sign of fear of war and the continuation of the confrontational approach of the Islamic Republic. He said the government's diplomatic efforts are more about buying time and deception than changing the approach and reaching an agreement.

After the elections, Benjamin Netanyahu will remain the Prime Minister of Israel until the formation of the new government. This post examines what limitations Israeli law imposes on Netanyahu in the transitional government regarding military operations.
In three work-related incidents in the cities of Mashhad, Kamyaran, and Qom, two workers died and one other worker was injured.
The police commander of Sabzevar reported the arrest of 40 citizens, including 15 women and 25 men, in this city due to holding an unauthorized and disruptive nighttime party.

Mehdi Tartaar, Persepolis coach, after victory over Nassaji said they are in the 11th week and he expects a championship in the third year of his contract. He spoke about team rejuvenation and former players' confidence and denied rumors of a dispute with Karim Bagheri. Tartaar emphasized that Karim Bagheri is like a brother to him and is the club's identity.

Fereshteh Pezeshk, an international relations expert, said Gulf Arab countries are trying through diplomatic efforts to contain the consequences of a possible war for their land and infrastructure. She said the wide gap between the positions of the Islamic Republic and the United States has made resolving the crisis through diplomacy difficult.

Abbas Araghchi confirmed the presence of the Iranian delegation in Doha but said there are no plans to meet with American officials. The media of the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic reported that Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered an immediate and geographically unrestricted response to potential attacks by the US and Israel. Reports indicate that Donald Trump is considering a large-scale military operation against Iran after the midterm elections.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, stated on the sidelines of the G20 summit that discussions about Iran are ongoing and Trump prefers the issue to be resolved peacefully. He also said that there are some issues that cannot be resolved peacefully, and if a diplomatic solution exists, the US would welcome it, but such a solution cannot jeopardize US national security. Rubio added that the Islamic Republic is seeking to become a nuclear-armed power and is at the center of all instability in the Middle East.

Rubio said we live in a world where a country openly states it will blow up commercial ships. He described this situation as a challenge for all countries in the region. Rubio compared this issue to conditions 80 or 100 years ago.
Mohsen Rezaei: Tone of Trump deputy's letter has changed, a sign Iran's authority is consolidated

A number of workers at the Iran Shahr steam power plant in Bampur county complain about unpaid wages and uncertainty about their job status and demand full payment of arrears and resolution of employment status for experienced workers. Maintenance workers of the railway line and technical structures in Lorestan railway area protested unpaid amounts related to war days and arrears of protective and livelihood equipment.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, wrote on X that the level of ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, except for Iranian oil shipments, has returned to pre-conflict levels. Bessent, on Saturday, 9 Aban, referring to Iran's oil exports, wrote: "The world can live without Iranian oil; but Iran cannot live without oil exports."

Halloween celebrations took place last night in various parts of Iran, with young people wearing special Halloween costumes and makeup in the streets. In some cities, including Tehran, the event turned into clashes between security forces and citizens. According to reports, Basij and plainclothes forces attacked the Halloween gathering on Iranshahr Street, and eyewitnesses said security forces dispersed the crowd by closing the street, evacuating and closing cafes, beating attendees, and arresting some of them.

Halloween celebrations were held last night in various parts of Iran, with young people wearing special Halloween costumes and makeup in the streets. In some cities, the celebration turned into clashes between security forces and citizens. An interview with Maryam Dehkordi, journalist and member of IranWire editorial team.
A report has been published about the largest theft in history, in which 6.3 billion dollars were stolen in 30 minutes.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that the stubbornness of Tehran and Washington and mutual threats have pushed tensions toward escalation. He described an order attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei for a response "without geographical limitation" as a threat against goals beyond the region.

On Saturday, 9 Aban, a group of private car drivers on the Minab to Bandar Abbas route protested at Esteghlal Square in Minab against insufficient gasoline quotas, increased fuel costs, and lack of fuel supply infrastructure.

The public and revolutionary prosecutor of Jask announced the formation of a judicial case and the issuance of summonses for several citizens due to the production and dissemination of clips contrary to public norms and religious and cultural values in cyberspace.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the representative of the Supreme Leader in Khorasan Razavi, said that today's issue is equipping against the enemy and intimidating it, and nuclear weapons are a source of intimidating the enemy. He added that the importance of acquiring nuclear weapons for greater deterrence against the enemy is received from various platforms and the demands of the people.

Harry Kane showed his 2026 Ballon d'Or to 75,000 spectators at Allianz Arena before the Bayern Munich vs Dortmund match. He entered the field wearing shoes with golden soles and the names of his four children. Five days after the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, Bayern Munich and the German Football League honored him again.

The Deputy of Tourism at Tehran's Cultural Heritage Organization reported identifying nearly 800 Instagram pages active in organizing unauthorized tourism tours and said documents have been submitted for legal action. He cited lack of insurance coverage and non-compliance with Islamic Republic laws as reasons for operating outside permitted frameworks. Footage of group dancing and celebrations in some tours indicates that social behaviors and violations are also targeted in these actions.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said if Trump and the US are not punished, other countries will consider attacking Iran futile. He added that if war starts, the US will suffer a severe blow and Iran's anti-ship missiles have been tested on the USS George Washington. Rezaee also said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions set by the Islamic Republic are met.

The US Central Command, CENTCOM, released an image of a US Navy helicopter taking off from the aircraft carrier George Washington and wrote on X that this ship supports the US naval blockade against the Islamic Republic. CENTCOM stated that US forces have altered the routes of 144 commercial ships until October 31 to ensure compliance with the blockade.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, said that the purchase and contract for Sukhoi-35 fighters had been pursued for a long time and pilot training had been completed. He added that after the war, the Air Force fleet will appear stronger. The army's plan is to buy advanced fighters and expand the fleet.

Reports indicate that a Chinese company, despite receiving Iranian oil, has not fulfilled its multi-billion dollar commitments to supply goods and services. The CEO of Iran Air said the company, despite committing to deliver 55 airplanes, has only delivered two old planes at prices several times the market rate. Ata Hosseinian said the simultaneous release of reports about oil trusts and Chinese companies' violations may be part of a guided process.

Fars News Agency reported that the Central Bank intends to exclude car and mobile phone importers from the official currency market. Ahmad Alavi, an economist, said this action will not solve the currency crisis and will lead to higher prices and lower product quality. He added that Iran's structural economic problems will not be resolved by such decisions and consumers will bear the highest costs.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, said that the countries involved in the four-party meeting with Iran had themselves requested to travel to Tehran. He added that the meeting did not discuss the Mecca Pact or Yemen but focused on future regional security arrangements. Rezaee also said the participants spoke firmly against Israel, and the Saudi defense minister stated that Israel would target Turkey and then Saudi Arabia after Iran.

Ata Mohamad said both the Islamic Republic and the US believe they can gain more concessions from the other side. He added that the main disagreements remain and there is no sign of an imminent agreement. Also, regional countries are increasing their diplomatic efforts with concern over the possible expansion of the war.

Yesterday, the football match between Malavan Bandar Anzali and Chadormalu Ardakan was held with female spectators present at Sirous Ghaeqran Stadium in Anzali due to a disciplinary committee ruling by the Football Federation, and men were not allowed to watch the match directly. The game ended with a 2-1 victory for Chadormalu.

The US midterm congressional elections could affect Washington's policy towards the Islamic Republic, but the decision to continue or end the war is up to the president. The Democrats' victory increases oversight, political pressure, and budgetary restrictions, but alone it does not mean the end of the war.

Ali Tajernia, chairman of Esteghlal's board, said two board members told him he would dismiss Sohrab Bakhtiyari-Zadeh by the fifth week, but he did not because he wanted to give an Esteghlali a chance and due to the country's conditions. Tajernia added that Bakhtiyari-Zadeh accepted coaching the team without any conditions, while two Iranian and two foreign candidates had heavy conditions. Bakhtiyari-Zadeh came after Mousimane and got good results for two weeks but left the team before the match against Persepolis and requested a foreign assistant, which was not approved.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that three days before the US midterm congressional elections, evidence indicates that the likelihood of an agreement has decreased and the US, Israel, and the Islamic Republic are rapidly moving toward a broad and intense war. He added that mutual threats have peaked and both sides are expressing their readiness for military confrontation. This war could inflict heavier blows on the military and political structure of the Islamic Republic.

Kambiz Tavana said Marco Rubio's positions indicate Washington seeks a fundamental change in the behavior and policies of the Islamic Republic and no longer considers broad agreements and diplomatic promises sufficient. He added that Qatari mediators have presented a seven-day proposal including seven specific steps to Tehran. According to Tavana, the US demands practical and implementable actions before advancing negotiations, while the Islamic Republic still insists on lifting sanctions and receiving concessions in exchange for an agreement.

Jamshid Barzegar said Mojtaba Khamenei's absence from public view has reduced the impact of threats attributed to him, but senior military commanders repeat these threats. He added Mohsen Rezaei, by raising the possibility of leaving the NPT and changing the nuclear doctrine, tries to increase pressure on the US and Western countries. Barzegar also said the Islamic Republic, by threatening to expand the war beyond the region, especially to Europe, wants European countries to pressure Washington to prevent a military attack, and the likelihood of a new military conflict has increased.

Gila Gamliel, Israel's Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, wrote in a message on X on the occasion of Prince Reza Pahlavi's birthday that last year's events left no doubt that the brave people of Iran, under his leadership, will free Iran. She added that this year, light will triumph over darkness, and Prince Reza Pahlavi will return to his homeland and shape his historic destiny in serving the people of Iran.

The Wall Street Journal reported, citing informed sources, that Trump spoke by phone with Netanyahu on Saturday morning to consult with his Middle Eastern ally as the US prepares to resume attacks on the Islamic Republic. This call came days after Trump held a meeting at the White House with senior military commanders about options for resuming extensive combat operations in the region. The Wall Street Journal also noted the political pressures facing both leaders.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, said in an interview with Kambiz Tavana that there has never been anything like the combination of sanctions and blockade against the Islamic Republic in history. Bessent added that the air and sea blockade of Iran is "impenetrable" and that the country faces the harshest economic isolation imposed by the US.

Donald Trump said at a Halloween party that they have destroyed Iran's nuclear capabilities and still need to clarify the status of one or two sites but can do it in 10 minutes. He expressed doubt about Tehran's reliability in negotiations and said Iran will never have nuclear weapons. Trump added that negotiations are going well but Iran is not very reliable and retreats after agreements.

Afrah Al-Zouba, Yemen's foreign minister, in a post on X called for the implementation of an arms embargo on the Houthis and an end to the Islamic Republic's support for this militia group. She described the siege of Taiz by the Houthis as a "war crime" and called for decisive international action to reopen the city's routes. Al-Zouba said Yemenis are defending their neighbors and global trade routes while trying to rebuild their government.

Ali Mamouri, a university professor and former Iraqi prime minister's advisor, said the seven-year war led by the Saudi coalition against the Houthis did not succeed, and considering the group's military capabilities and geographic position, there is no option left but "negotiation" and "agreement."

Siamak Aram, a political analyst, referred to a message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei and said that the continuation of the crisis could help the Islamic Republic cover internal problems, intensify repression, and buy time.

Kambiz Tavana, a member of Iran International's editorial team, referred to statements by Donald Trump and Marco Rubio, saying diplomatic efforts continue, but both speak of the limitations of this path.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi warned about the imminent risk of execution for Shahab Zahdi, a protester arrested in Dey month and imprisoned in Qezel Hesar prison in Alborz. Shahab Zahdi was first sentenced to death in Bahman 1404, but the Supreme Court of the Islamic Republic later overturned this sentence. Four other citizens were executed in the same case, and Shahab Zahdi is now again at imminent risk of execution.

Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, called for a swift resolution of the dispute between the US and the Islamic Republic on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta. He said the closure of this strait has severely increased global economic pressures by disrupting energy supply and international trade.

Navid Mohibi, a political analyst, referring to the report of the Trump-Netanyahu call, said the US sees negotiating with the main decision-makers of the Islamic Republic as a way to test the possibility of an agreement, but Israel views these individuals as obstacles to the agreement and seeks to remove them and "peel away" the power structure.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic stated in a statement that it has listed the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force of Britain as "terrorist" organizations and the British foreign intelligence service, MI6, as a "hostile group." This decision was described as a reaction to Britain's military cooperation with the US and Israel over the past year. The responsibility for the consequences of this decision lies with the British government.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said the Islamic Republic wants an agreement but is not reliable in its commitments. He referred to the remaining "one or two" nuclear targets, including Mount Kolang, and said the US could attack them "within 10 minutes."

Iranian protests in Stockholm have entered their eleventh month. According to the organizers, these protests have continued uninterrupted in opposition to executions, suppression of protesters, political arrests, and human rights violations in Iran.

The Chazabeh border crossing between Iran and Iraq remains closed, and the official protest of the Islamic Republic has so far not changed Baghdad's decision. Protests against the closure of this crossing continue in Maysan province in Iraq, and groups close to Tehran are demanding its immediate reopening. Iraqi officials have cited technical and security problems as the reason for the border closure.

Mohsen Araki, a member of the Leadership Experts Assembly, called for a review of the Islamic Republic's membership in the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) during his advanced jurisprudence class. He said the Islamic Republic has suffered many damages due to this membership and has not gained proportional benefits. Araki also urged officials to place this demand on their agenda.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, called the orders of Mojtaba Khamenei, leader of the Islamic Republic, "final" and said they will respond to any threat immediately and more harshly than before. Azizi added that they determine the end of the war, not the losers of the 12-day and 40-day wars. The leader's media reported that Mojtaba Khamenei emphasized that any level and type of threat must be met with an immediate and impactful response without geographical limitation.

Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of the parliament, said in a speech before the session on Sunday, 10 Aban, that the window for nuclear negotiations is now closed to the enemy because they have nothing new to offer Iran. He warned that if the enemies commit another aggression, the remaining windows might also be closed and emphasized that the wisest action is to accept the realities and unconditionally implement the seven conditions of the Islamic Republic. Nikzad added that if the enemies repeat their mistake, as emphasized in yesterday's meeting of Khamenei with senior military commanders, they will face an immediate, effective, and geographically unrestricted response.

Rouhollah Rahimpour, a political analyst, referred to the report of a call between Trump and Netanyahu and said that if the war resumes, the likelihood of it starting a few days after the US midterm elections is higher, and the military and nuclear infrastructure of the Islamic Republic will be prioritized in potential attacks.

On the early morning of Sunday, 10 Aban, the execution sentence of a prisoner named Iman Ashraf was carried out in Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. The prisoner had previously been sentenced to death for murder. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency.
Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, warned that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, by disrupting energy supply and international trade, has increased pressure on the global economy.

Qatar Gas Transport Company "Nakilat" announced that a liquefied natural gas carrier named "Al Mayeda" was attacked by "unknown objects" on Friday evening while moving in the Persian Gulf. The company added that none of the crew were injured and the incident had no environmental impact. The ship is in a safe condition and the assessment of the consequences of the incident is ongoing.
Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in the UK commemorated Cyrus the Great and the Pahlavi kings on Saturday, 9 Aban.
The police commander of Abadan reported the closure of a clothing store in the city due to the installation of obscene and satanic signs.

Nasrollah Pejmanfar, head of the Parliament's Article 90 Commission, stated in a public session on Sunday, November 1, 2026, that the issue of withdrawing from the NPT should be seriously on the agenda, expressing hope that this decision would be made in obedience to Mojtaba Khamenei. Pejmanfar said he hopes this decision will come to fruition and that everyone will decide, in obedience to the leadership, to withdraw from the NPT to make them understand that Iran will not back down in the face of these pressures. He added that every time Grossi and the NPT team entered Iran, the country suffered significant damage and harm.
Videos received show a group of retired steelworkers in Isfahan gathered on Sunday, 10 Aban, protesting livelihood problems and shouted: "Our enemy is right here, they lie that it is America."

Peyvand and Borna Naeimi, Baha'i citizens imprisoned in Kerman prison, were sentenced to imprisonment by the fifth branch of the Revolutionary Court of this city. Peyvand Naeimi was sentenced to 12 years, six months, and one day, and Borna Naeimi to eight years in prison.

The International Testing Agency announced that Poneh Akhoundtabar Mazandarani, known as Tina Akhoundtabar, has been banned from sports competitions for three years due to a positive doping test and admission of the violation. The sample taken from her on December 6, 2024, during the "Boxing Champions Night" competition in Dubai contained the prohibited substance clenbuterol. The ban starts on February 20, 2025, and lasts until February 19, 2028, and her results in these competitions have been annulled.

Afrooz Eslam Panah, the mother of the late Behboud Hassanzadeh, passed away on 8 Aban. Behboud Hassanzadeh was 37 years old, held a master's degree in law, and was the father of two daughters. Behboud was killed by a war bullet on 18 Dey 404 in Kouhchenar, Fars, while helping one of the wounded.

Hossein Samsami, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission, said that the currency for essential goods is increasing by 1,000 tomans daily and that the country's economic conditions will worsen within a month. He added that the Ministry of Industry, Mine and Trade sent a letter to the Central Bank to supply only a few items at the rate of 188,000 tomans, while other goods will be supplied near the free market rate. Samsami warned that the prices of more than four thousand goods will deliberately increase by 100,000 tomans and that prices of goods and cars will rise by 40 to 50 percent in the next one or two months.

Israel's Channel 12 reported on Sunday, November 1, 2026, that signs of a potential resumption of war with Iran are increasing daily. Raz Zimet, head of the Iran program at Israel's Institute for National Security Studies, told the channel that in his opinion, only a few days or at most a few weeks remain until Trump concludes that waiting for Iran's response is futile. Zimet also estimated that the Islamic Republic currently possesses about 1,500 ballistic missiles, and in the event of another confrontation, Israeli cities would again be targeted by these missiles.
A video published on social media shows a baker calling the rationed flour sent to him "low quality" and saying, "This flour is weak and cannot be used to bake bread."

Various cities in France witnessed protests on the evening of Saturday, 9 Aban, against rising living costs and declining quality of public services. These gatherings had fewer participants and limited violence compared to previous weeks. Students, trade union members, and fewer yellow vest protesters demonstrated against fuel price hikes, inflation, and the policies of Emmanuel Macron's government.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, said Iran is fully prepared to respond to the US even outside West Asia and that Iran controls the timing of any potential future war's end. He warned that any renewed US aggression will face an immediate and broader response and added that US facilities and interests anywhere could be targeted. He also emphasized that the future war could be longer and the US president will not be able to determine its end time.

The news website Ynet reported that the Israeli army has completed its preparations for a new round of conflict with the Islamic Republic, and the start of operations depends on the decision of Donald Trump, the President of the United States. Political and military coordination between Israel and the US continues, and Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, has reviewed operational scenarios in various meetings.

Today, Sunday 10 Aban, a group of retired steel industry workers in Isfahan held a protest gathering in the city. The protest was against the performance of the supplementary insurance "Dana", issues related to medical services, incomplete implementation of salary adjustments, and other livelihood demands of these citizens.

Today, Sunday, a group of Social Security retirees protested in front of the organization's buildings in the cities of Shush and Ahvaz. Their demands include improving living conditions, increasing salaries and purchasing power, controlling inflation and price hikes, creating job opportunities, reducing housing rents, and access to free education, healthcare, and social services.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said that until the seven clauses announced by the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council are implemented, they will not enter negotiations with Washington. He added that at this stage, they cannot easily accept negotiations and until these conditions are operational, there will be no negotiations with the Americans. Kowsari also said that Americans have not adhered to their commitments in previous negotiations, and for this reason, they are not optimistic about the US.

Mehrdad Akhlaghi, the Minister of Defense of the Islamic Republic, announced that the ministry is pursuing the enhancement of intelligent combat readiness and the implementation of a strategy for immediate, effective, and proportionate response to any threat.
